As far as minimum wage goes, I don't think it's unreasonable to tell companies if they want to do business in this city their employees should be able to afford living in that city. There just needs to be a standard of living conditions and travel distances. Cities will be forced to balance cost of living with business growth. If cost of living is too high, businesses won't be able to afford living wages. I'd also be interested to see wages set by a profit sharing system. Every employee is paid in relation to the companies earnings and employee evaluations. There'd be a more direct relationship between employees quality of work and their salary, plus businesses wouldn't be expected to pay what they can't afford. It would be similar to investing, growth vs value.

This is also why I lean towards needs being under the public umbrella. There are two ways to cover cost of living, increases wages or decrease costs. If publicly funded needs significantly reduce costs, then cost of living is easier to achieve. Plus it would free up more sending money that will stimulate a wider range of the economy. But I'd only support going publicly if there was that significant cost reduction for everyone.
